title: Origins and Molecular Features of a Chimeric Type‐P4A ATPase—Guanylate Cyclase from Stramenopiles and Alveolates
content: A chimeric protein produced from the fusion of a type-P4 ATPase, also called flippase, and a guanylate cyclase (P4GC) was originally described in ciliates and malaria parasites. An extensive search for P4GC homologues was carried out and structural features of the pro-tein were determined by sequence alignments and homology modeling. P4GC is found in all alveolate lineages and in some stramenopile lineages. This suggests that the gene fu-sion event occurred before the divergence of stramenopiles and alveolates, but after the di-vergence of rhizarians and stramenopiles. This scenario necessitates the subsequent loss of P4GC in some stramenopile lineages. Alternatively, and perhaps the more favorable ex-planation, the gene fusion occurred in an alveolate progenitor before diversification of cil-iates, dinoflagellates, and apicomplexans and then a horizontal gene transfer event oc-curred in a progenitor of oomycetes and bicosoecids, or vice versa. The sequence homology of the flippase module is not well preserved in some lineages, whereas the structure and sequence homology of the cyclase module is highly conserved in all lineages. Thus, P4GC may function primarily as a guanylate cyclase and secondarily as a flippase in some line-ages. However, the predicted 3-dimensional structure of the flippase module is highly conserved in all lineages and P4GC likely plays a supportive role in the function of the cyclase module. Furthermore, P4GC may have distinct roles in the various stramenopile and alveolate lineages.
